Dial Studio

Design rose-engine and straight-line patterns, export for CAD and CNC

Design

Bodies

Each body is a separate plate with its own outline and its own layers, like a sub-dial or an applied plaque. The top of the list sits on top. Height moves a body up or down: 0 is flush with the base, negative sinks it in, and a body set into the one below gets a pocket cut for it.

    Body

    Saved in this browser

      Designs saved here stay in this browser on this device, uploaded fonts included. Saving again under the same design name updates that save. To move a design to another device or keep a backup, use Download design.

      Presets

      A preset sets the whole design: layers, cut depth, graver angle, export settings, and the 3D finish and thickness. It replaces the current design; you can undo it right after.

      Layers

      The top layer is drawn over the ones below. A layer set to hide layers below cuts a clean window, for sub-dials and chapter rings. Holes cut through everything. Double-click a name, or use ✎, to rename it.

        Cut and export

        Fusion model (3D dial)

        Fusion model downloads a .zip with a Fusion script and your design data. Install the script once (Shift+S in Fusion, then + next to My Scripts), run it, pick the data file and type the dial thickness. It builds the dial body with every hole cut through, draws the pattern on the top face, and can cut each line in as a real V-groove using the graver angle and depth above. Grooves are slow: fine for a few hundred lines, very slow for thousands. The README in the zip has the steps.

        DXF into Fusion

        1. Export DXF. It downloads as a .zip (compressed, and allowed everywhere the app runs); unzip it.
        2. In Fusion, use Insert > Insert DXF on the dial's top face. Pick millimetres and one sketch per layer. Big layers are already split into numbered parts so each sketch stays small.
        3. Don't model the grooves as 3D cuts. In Manufacture, use 2D > Trace on the sketches with a V-bit or chamfer mill, and set the axial offset to minus the cut depth.
        4. Only visible layers are exported, so you can hide layers and export in batches.
        5. With several bodies, Export SVG and Export DXF give the selected body, centred on its own origin, since each body is machined as its own part. Fusion model builds every visible body in place.
